public_rationale: On 2025-08-20, Marcus wrote that the mania for LLMs "would break eventually." He gave no deadline. Around the same time, Sam Altman said he thought investors were overexcited about AI (e3). That supports the idea that there was a mania, but it does not show whether it later broke. Nvidia reported revenue of $96.2 billion for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, up 106% from a year earlier. Its data center revenue was $89.0 billion, up 117% (e1). On 2026-08-27, Nvidia's CEO called the AI infrastructure buildout "at full steam" (e2). The early-resolution rule needs Nvidia data center revenue or combined hyperscaler AI capital spending to fall more than 30% year over year for two or more quarters in a row. The evidence shows growth through July 2026, so that rule is not met. The packet has nothing on the period after that quarter. Because the forecast has no deadline, the lack of a collapse in the evidence does not count against it. The forecast stays open.
limitations: The latest market data in the packet covers the quarter ended July 26, 2026. It cannot show whether a collapse began between then and the 2026-10-28 evaluation date.
The packet has no data on hyperscaler AI capital spending, AI startup funding or valuations, or AI-linked stock indices.
The market evidence comes from a single company, Nvidia. The CEO's statement is the company's own view.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The mania for LLMs will eventually break.

statement.excerpt: For the last few years, I have been warning you that the mania for LLMs would break eventually.
statement.document_title: Is this the moment when the Generative AI bubble finally deflates?

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at some point, enthusiasm for LLMs would visibly collapse. That means a sharp, sustained fall in generative AI investment, AI chip and data center spending, and AI-linked valuations, not a short dip.
He gave no deadline ('eventually'), so this is an open-horizon forecast. The lack of a collapse before the evaluation date does not count against him.
criteria.support_condition: A dated, decisive collapse of the LLM boom: for example, AI data center or chip spending falling steeply year over year for several quarters, major AI valuations or funding rounds collapsing, and widespread reporting that the boom has ended.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, the forecast cannot be shown false at a fixed date. Continued strong growth only shows the break has not happened yet.

evidence.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. reported record revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago.
evidence.locator: Summary, first paragraph after bullet points
evidence.explanation: The main seller of AI chips more than doubled its revenue year over year into mid-2026. That shows the LLM investment boom had not broken by then. It does not refute an open-ended forecast.

evidence.explanation: Nvidia's CEO described the AI buildout as still accelerating in August 2026. This is a company view, but it is consistent with the reported revenue.

evidence.explanation: Even Altman said investors were overexcited around the time of the post. That backs the premise that there was a mania, but says nothing about whether it later broke.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated company filings or reputable financial reporting showing a sustained collapse would resolve this. For example: Nvidia data center revenue or combined hyperscaler AI capital spending falling more than 30% year over year for two or more quarters in a row, together with broad reporting that generative AI investment has collapsed. That would support the forecast. Because there is no deadline, no fixed date can contradict it.
